gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Keychron's own spec line gives the K3 HE (sold as its 'best wireless magnetic option') a 1,000 Hz polling rate in every connection mode (2.4 GHz, Bluetooth and wired), or that Keychron makes the cheaper K3 Max switch-swappable only in its 'RGB Backlight Hot-Swappable Version' and only with Gateron low-profile MX mechanical switches.
standout_why: I could not check this properly against the rival pages. The RTINGS low-profile roundup (rtings.com/keyboard/reviews/best/low-profile) returned only its title and navigation, with no picks or spec text. NuPhy.com and pay.nuphy.com (both cited) returned HTTP 429 on all four tries. I did not open geekgamingtricks, dejaflow, mkbguide or Tom's Hardware. In ChatGPT's own answer, the 8,000 Hz figure appears only on the NuPhy card. Its K3 HE card says 'Rapid Trigger, 2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, and wired' and gives no polling rate. The K3 Max card says '1,000Hz polling over wired/2.4GHz' and does not mention the hot-swap limit to one version. A roundup could easily repeat Keychron's 1,000 Hz spec line, so I am scoring this 1, not 2.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's FPS pick of the wired NuPhy Air75 HE, though I could not open NuPhy's page to confirm its 8,000 Hz claim. Going wireless with the K3 HE means 1,000 Hz in every mode, even plugged in. For the K3 Max 'best value' pick, a shopper who wants to swap switches must buy the RGB hot-swappable version, and it takes low-profile MX mechanical switches, not magnetic ones. Because the K3 HE uses LSA-profile keycaps, Keychron's LSA PBT keycap set fits it, but the same set does not fit the original K3.
